questions.question: Which tennis legend is this?
questions.explanation: Serena Williams won 23 Grand Slam singles titles, more than any other woman since tennis turned professional in 1968.

media.alt: A smiling tennis player on court

questions.question: Which gymnast is this?
questions.explanation: Several moves in the gymnastics rulebook are named after Biles, because she was the first to land them in competition.

media.alt: A smiling gymnast in a red team jacket

questions.question: Which tennis legend is this?
questions.explanation: Federer won the Wimbledon men's singles a record eight times.

media.alt: A tennis player wearing a headband

questions.question: Basketball legend Michael Jordan famously wore which shirt number?
questions.explanation: Jordan won six NBA titles with the Chicago Bulls, and his first Air Jordan trainers came out in 1985.

questions.question: Which darts legend was nicknamed 'The Power'?
questions.explanation: Taylor, from Stoke-on-Trent, won 16 world championships.

questions.question: Which snooker legend is nicknamed 'The Rocket'?
questions.explanation: He earned the nickname for his lightning-fast play, once making a maximum break in five minutes and eight seconds.

questions.question: Sir Chris Hoy won six Olympic gold medals in which sport?
questions.explanation: Hoy grew up in Edinburgh, and the velodrome in Glasgow is named after him.

questions.question: Wayne Gretzky, known as 'The Great One', is a legend of which sport?
questions.explanation: His shirt number, 99, was retired by every team in the NHL, so nobody can wear it again.

questions.question: Sachin Tendulkar, nicknamed 'the Little Master', played cricket for which country?
questions.explanation: Tendulkar was the first player to score 100 international centuries.

questions.question: Which Dutch football legend gave his name to a famous trick, first seen at the 1974 World Cup?
questions.explanation: The Cruyff turn drags the ball behind the standing leg, and it left a Swedish defender going the wrong way.

questions.question: Which tennis player is known as 'the King of Clay'?
questions.explanation: Nadal won the French Open, played on clay courts in Paris, a record 14 times.

questions.question: In 2012, Bradley Wiggins became the first British rider to win which famous race?
questions.explanation: Just ten days after finishing in Paris, he won Olympic gold in the time trial in London.

questions.question: In 2019, Eliud Kipchoge became the first person to run a marathon in under how long?
questions.explanation: He ran 1 hour 59 minutes 40 seconds in Vienna, though it was a special event with pacemakers, so it is not an official record.

questions.question: Jonah Lomu, the giant winger who ran through defenders at the 1995 Rugby World Cup, played for which country?
questions.explanation: He scored four tries against England in the semi-final.

questions.question: Babe Ruth was a legend of which sport?
questions.explanation: Ruth hit 60 home runs for the New York Yankees in 1927, a record that stood for 34 years.

questions.question: Which boxing legend is this, pictured as a young man?
questions.explanation: Ali called himself The Greatest and promised to 'float like a butterfly, sting like a bee'.

media.alt: A black-and-white portrait of a young man

questions.question: Which Brazilian football legend is this?
questions.explanation: Pelé is the only player to have won the World Cup three times: 1958, 1962 and 1970.

media.alt: A footballer in a yellow shirt with a green collar

questions.question: Martina Navratilova won the Wimbledon women's singles a record how many times?
questions.explanation: Six of her titles came in a row, from 1982 to 1987.

questions.question: Which golfer was nicknamed 'the Golden Bear'?
questions.explanation: Nicklaus won 18 major championships, still the most by any man at the end of 2025.

questions.question: Carl Lewis won Olympic gold at four Games in a row, from 1984 to 1996, in which event?
questions.explanation: In all, Lewis won nine Olympic gold medals in sprinting and jumping.

questions.question: Eddy Merckx, the cyclist nicknamed 'the Cannibal' for wanting to win everything, came from which country?
questions.explanation: Merckx won the Tour de France five times, and in 1969 took the overall, points and mountains prizes in the same Tour.

questions.question: To which piece of music did Torvill and Dean skate to Olympic gold in 1984?
questions.explanation: All nine judges gave them a perfect 6.0 for artistic impression.

questions.question: Shane Warne's 'Ball of the Century' in 1993 bowled out which England batsman?
questions.explanation: It was Warne's very first ball in a Test in England, and it spun sharply to clip the top of off stump.

questions.question: What is Tiger Woods's real first name?
questions.explanation: His father, Earl, nicknamed him Tiger after a fellow soldier who had saved his life in the Vietnam War.

questions.question: Daley Thompson won Olympic gold in 1980 and 1984 in which ten-event contest?
questions.explanation: He famously whistled along to the national anthem on the podium in Los Angeles.

questions.question: Which Brazilian striker, nicknamed 'O Fenômeno', scored both goals in the 2002 World Cup final?
questions.explanation: Brazil beat Germany 2–0 in Yokohama, four years after Ronaldo was taken ill on the day of the 1998 final.

questions.question: In 2004, who became the first batsman to score 400 in a Test innings?
questions.explanation: Lara made 400 not out against England in Antigua, ten years after scoring 375 against them on the same ground.

questions.question: Who won the 1985 World Snooker Championship final on the very last black, watched by 18.5 million people on BBC Two?
questions.explanation: Taylor beat Steve Davis just after midnight, in one of the most watched broadcasts in BBC Two history.

questions.question: In 1996, Frankie Dettori rode all seven winners on a single day at which racecourse?
questions.explanation: The 'Magnificent Seven' came at combined odds of 25,095 to 1 and cost bookmakers millions.

questions.question: Gareth Edwards scored 'that try' for the Barbarians in 1973 against which team?
questions.explanation: The move began deep in the Barbarians' own half and is often called the greatest try ever scored.
